title: Operate and Integrate Inventory
readerIntent: Secure, monitor, recover, and qualify Inventory.
priorKnowledge: Understand all Inventory models and external integrations.
summary: Operations correlate balances, movements, reservations, allocations, transfers, sourcing, reconciliation, publication, cache, search, and external evidence.

sections.heading: Operate
items: Monitor balance/movement throughput, reservation expiry, allocation failure, sourcing misses, transfer age, reconciliation variance, cache invalidation, publication lag, and provider health.
Secure lifecycle routes, tenant/store/warehouse scope, service identities, external source aliases, and sensitive location/business data.
Recover unknown outcomes through idempotency and reconciliation; never guess by replaying an unsafe movement.
Load-test high-contention products, zones, warehouses, unit conversion, publication, cache, and distributed topology.

sections.heading: Security and authority
items: Authorize every movement, reservation, allocation, transfer, reconciliation, and configuration operation.
Resolve tenant, enterprise, Store, warehouse, pool, product, and service context on the backend.
Separate employee, service, scheduled, and external integration identities.
Protect location, capacity, commercial policy, and personal data.
Audit adjustments, manual runs, replays, and overrides.

sections.heading: Performance and scale
items: Partition high-contention balances deliberately.
Use bounded atomic or revision behavior.
Keep availability computation and cache keys context-complete.
Rate-limit reconciliation, expiry, import, and publication batches.
Load-test flash events, popular products, many zones, fractional units, and distributed nodes.

sections.heading: Incident examples
items: Oversell risk: stop affected reservations, reconcile movements and holds, and repair through governed adjustments.
Stale availability: inspect publication, movement, invalidation, provider, and context key.
Unknown movement outcome: query by idempotency identity before retry.
Expired-reservation backlog: bound recovery and protect hot balances.
Transfer discrepancy: preserve dispatch and receipt evidence and start reconciliation.

sections.heading: Recovery and continuity
paragraphs: Restart rebuilds disposable schedules and caches from persisted definitions and authoritative inventory. Provider or node failure never makes in-memory state the balance authority.
External integrations resume from stable source identities and reconciliation windows. Unsafe writes are not replayed blindly.

sections.heading: Production readiness
items: Contention, load, soak, node loss, partition, restart, and recovery.
Unit precision and conversion boundaries.
Tenant and service-scope isolation.
Cache and search provider qualification.
Publishing staged-to-online and external-system reconciliation.
Dashboards, alerts, runbooks, backup, audit, and accountable ownership.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How To Operate And Integrate Inventory
paragraphs: Operations teams and BackOffice users can inspect Stock Balances, Movements, Reservations, Allocations, Transfers, and reconciliation findings through dedicated read-only Inventory endpoints. A user needs the `inventory.operations.read` permission. The endpoints are paged and return only safe operational fields.
Developers must use the relevant command API to change Stock. The operational pages are not editable database screens.

sections.heading: Check and reconstruct on-hand Stock
paragraphs: A scheduled service can create an immutable Movement checkpoint when a Balance has no pending Movement. Later, Inventory can replay the contiguous applied Movement revisions after that checkpoint and compare the expected on-hand quantity and revision with the current Balance.

This process does not reconstruct Reservation state. Use reconciliation findings and Reservation evidence for held quantities. If a revision is missing or out of order, investigate the history instead of forcing a correction.

sections.heading: Connect a WMS or POS
paragraphs: Inventory providers are disabled by default. An administrator configures a named WMS or POS provider that points to a Nodics connector module and lists its allowed operations. The connector module owns remote URLs and credentials.

Internal callers send an idempotency key, configured provider code, allowed operation, and bounded payload. Inventory records the attempt and outcome. A provider response never changes Stock directly; receipts, issues, transfers, and corrections still pass through Stock Movement.

sections.heading: Multi-hop Units
paragraphs: Units can optionally convert through multiple exact conversion rules when no direct rule exists. Keep this disabled unless the business maintains a governed conversion graph. Nodics selects one shortest path; competing shortest paths fail instead of choosing silently.
